newsitem.title: UK: Blair-UK stopped majority EU voting in key areas.
newsitem.headline: Blair-UK stopped majority EU voting in key areas.

text.p: British Prime Minister Tony Blair said on Wednesday he was able to stop the extension of majority voting on European Union matters where it was not in Britain's interests because of his positive approach to Europe.

"We have prevented the extension of qualified majority voting where it might cause damage," he told parliament, particularly in the Social Chapter which guarantees certain minimum rights for employees.
"Others wanted to extended QMV in the Social Chapter, which would have affected our companies even if we were not party to the Chapter. Because we were in it, we were able to stop this," Blair said.
The Prime Minister returned from an Amsterdam summit of EU leaders earlier on Wednesday.

His Labour government committed itself to sign the EU's Social Chapter within days of taking power on May 1. The previous Conservative government had refused to sign, saying the restrictions would cost jobs.
Blair said he had agreed to extend QMV in other areas where it was in its Britain's interests.

Earlier, he said all of his demands had been met in Amsterdam, with Britain's border controls guaranteed, a deal secured to keep NATO as the pillar of Europe's defence and an agreement on how to deal with quota-hopping fishing fleets.
In parliament, he pledged to keep up the pressure to complete the Single Market, opening up Europe to free and fair competition.
"This should in time lead to further opening of Europe's markets to British companies. Completing the single market will be one of the top priorities of the British presidency."
Britain will take up the EU Presidency for the first six months of next year.
